title: CapturePack manifest.json
description: Schema for manifest.json, the REQUIRED entry point of a CapturePack (format 0.1.0). It identifies the pack, records the capture environment, and inventories the variable parts of the pack (replay video, plugin payloads). Unknown additional properties are deliberately allowed everywhere: readers MUST accept unknown optional fields for forward compatibility (SPEC.md §13). See SPEC.md §5 for the normative definition; where schema and prose disagree, the prose wins.

format.description: Format marker. MUST be the literal string "capturepack". The first thing a reader checks to identify the file.

format_version.description: Version of the CapturePack specification this pack conforms to, as semver (e.g. "0.1.0"). Writers SHOULD write the oldest version that fully expresses their content. Major (pre-1.0: minor) version changes are breaking; see SPEC.md §13.

id.description: RFC 4122 UUID uniquely identifying this pack. Version 4 (random) RECOMMENDED, lowercase RECOMMENDED.

created_at.description: Capture instant as ISO 8601 date-time. A timezone designator (offset or 'Z') MUST be present — local wall-clock time is context. Example: "2026-07-27T14:03:21+09:00".

generator.description: The software that wrote this pack.

name.description: Name of the generating tool, e.g. "capturepack".

version.description: Version of the generating tool. Note: this is the tool's version, not the format version.

title.description: OPTIONAL short human-readable title, one line. Used as the report.md heading and recommended as the basis of the pack filename.

note.description: OPTIONAL user-written intent, verbatim: what the user was doing, what they expected, what went wrong. Carried into report.md unchanged. The single most valuable field for an LLM reading the pack.

environment.description: Where the capture happened. Describes the hardware/OS environment; it does not define the annotation coordinate space (annotations are always in snapshot pixel coordinates, SPEC.md §8.2).

os.description: Operating system family, lowercase. Recommended values: "windows", "macos", "linux". Other values allowed for other platforms.

os_version.description: OPTIONAL (recommended) free-form OS version, e.g. "11 Pro 26200" or "14.5".

screens.description: OPTIONAL (recommended) list of displays present at capture time, in OS enumeration order.

scale.description: OS display scale factor (1, 1.25, 1.5, 2, ...). Default 1 when absent.

app.description: OPTIONAL name of the application that had focus at capture time, e.g. "notably.exe" or "Google Chrome". Plugins can attach richer window/app data under plugins/.

media.description: Declares the pack's media files. Readers MUST take the replay filename from media.replay rather than probing the pack for files.

snapshot.description: Filename of the snapshot image. In format 0.1.0 this MUST be "snapshot.png". Declared explicitly so future format versions can vary it without breaking readers that trust the manifest.

replay.description: Filename of the replay video — "replay.webm" (recommended; MediaRecorder output, no extra dependencies) or "replay.mp4" — or null for a screenshot-only pack. A pack contains at most one replay file.

replay_duration_ms.description: Duration of the replay video in milliseconds. REQUIRED (as an integer) when replay is a filename; MUST be null or absent when replay is null.

replay_annotated.description: OPTIONAL filename of the annotated replay — "replay_annotated.webm" or "replay_annotated.mp4" — the replay with annotation boxes (blur, border, number badge, text) rendered into the pixels, playable in any player and always regenerable from replay + annotations.json (SPEC.md §7.2). MUST be absent when replay is null (nothing to render it from), and absent while the annotated replay has not (yet) been rendered. The annotated replay may render in the background after save, so readers MAY encounter a manifest declaring this file before the file exists — treat that as 'still rendering' and fall back to replay + annotations.json.

snapshot_t_ms.description: OPTIONAL position in the replay timeline, in milliseconds, of the frame shown in snapshot.png — the same clock as timeline t_ms offsets relative to t0 (SPEC.md §10.1). Absent means the snapshot is the capture instant (the native 'now' frame). SHOULD be absent when replay is null: without a replay there is no timeline to anchor the value to. See SPEC.md §7.1 (frame-accurate captures).

replay_duration_ms.description: When a replay file is declared, its duration in milliseconds is required and must be an integer.
When replay is null (screenshot-only pack), replay_duration_ms must be null if present.

replay_annotated.description: When replay is null there is nothing to render an annotated replay from — replay_annotated MUST be absent (SPEC.md §5.3).

plugins.description: OPTIONAL inventory of plugin payload directories under plugins/. Absent or empty means no plugin data. Every plugin directory written by the exporter must have an entry here; readers MUST ignore plugin directories they do not recognize (SPEC.md §11).

name.description: Plugin name: lowercase letters, digits, single hyphens; no leading/trailing hyphen. Must equal the directory name under plugins/ and the name in that directory's meta.json.

version.description: Plugin version (semver recommended). Must equal the version in the plugin's meta.json.

path.description: Directory path relative to the pack root, with trailing slash. Must be exactly "plugins/<name>/" where <name> is this entry's name field (equality with name cannot be expressed in JSON Schema; see SPEC.md §5.4).
